cards.text: This is a prayer from David, the shepherd boy (1 Samuel 16:11) who became Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), written when he was in the cave. And friend, he is NOT whispering in there. He cries aloud and lifts his voice to the LORD.

cards.question: David lifts his voice to the LORD from that cave. What is he asking for?

cards.text: Now David's got a complaint and some trouble weighing on him. And the big question is what he DOES with it, because some of us just smile real wide and say 'I'm FINE' while the whole oven's on fire.

cards.question: True or false: David keeps his trouble to himself and hides it from the LORD.

cards.text: David admits his spirit grows faint within him, phone-at-2% faint. But with that last little bit of battery, he tells the LORD one thing.

cards.question: True or false: Even as his spirit grows faint, David tells the LORD that He knows David's way.

cards.text: Then David talks about the path he travels. Somebody has hidden something along it, and I promise you, baker, it is NOT a welcome mat.

cards.question: What has been hidden along the path David travels?

cards.text: Next, David asks the LORD to look to his right and see.

cards.question: When the LORD looks to David's right, what does David say is there?
True or false: Looking around, David says there is no refuge for him and no one cares for his soul.

cards.text: So David turns and cries out to the LORD. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know the exact moment you stop looking AROUND and start looking UP.

cards.question: Nobody around David cares for his soul. Now he tells the LORD that He is his ___.

cards.text: David adds that the LORD is his portion in the land of the living. Then he asks the LORD to listen to his cry, because he's been brought quite low, and he asks to be rescued from the people chasing him.

cards.question: David asks to be rescued from his pursuers because they are too ___ for him.

cards.text: Last line of the prayer. David reaches for one more picture of where his soul is stuck.

cards.question: What does David ask the LORD to free his soul from?
David wants his soul set free so that he may ___ the LORD's name.
The man with nobody at his right hand pictures people gathering around him. Who does David say will gather?
True or false: David says the righteous will gather around him because of his own courage.

findings.problem: The story card is one flat sentence that only restates Psalm 142:4's opening. It has no Papa Dorin voice and little context to set up the question on card 10.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card packs three separate things into one card: the LORD as his portion in the land of the living (v5), the plea to listen because he is brought quite low (v6), and the request to be rescued from his pursuers (v6).

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The card says 'Last line of the prayer,' but verse 7 has several lines: free my soul from prison, that I may praise Your name, and the righteous will gather. Three more choice cards (17 to 20) still come from it. What he points out is not accurate.

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The passage ends on a true-or-false card whose right answer is False. The baker learns the reason is not David's own courage, but no card ever says the actual reason in Psalm 142:7: 'because of Your goodness to me.' That detail is the turning point of the psalm's ending, and it's never told or asked.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
